title: How to Keep Your Digital Accounts Secure
body_text: As Americans become more reliant on the Internet, cybersecurity threats also continue to surge. In 2017, there were 16.7 million identity fraud victims1 – this represents an increase of one million victims over one year alone. Among these victims were consumers who had their account credentials stolen. Dubbed account takeover, this type of fraud involves a hacker using valid account information to extract funds or purchase new products and services. Account takeover fraud reached an all-time high in 2017 with $5.1 billion in losses .1 As account takeover continues to rise, how do consumers protect themselves? While you might be tempted to go “off-the-grid” by reducing as many digital accounts as possible, this response is impractical. Because of the ubiquitous usage of the Internet, your account information is stored online, regardless of whether you conduct your activities online. Instead, we recommend a multi-layered approach to cybersecurity – in other words, defense in depth. By setting up multiple layers of protection, you will decrease the likelihood and magnitude of account takeover fraud. In this article, we’ll review six strategies for keeping your digital accounts secure. This should be common sense. Unfortunately, many Americans still use easy-to-guess credentials. For example – SplashData analyzes millions of passwords from leaked data breaches to produce its annual Worst Passwords List. The top three passwords of 2017? 123456, password, and 123456782. Not only are these passwords incredibly easy to guess, but they have also remained unchanged for the past six years . Using weak passwords isn’t just foolish, it’s also incredibly counteractive to keeping your account information secure. How to Create a Strong Password Make sure your password is long (at least 12 characters) with a string of random numbers, capital and lowercase letters, and symbols. While it’s okay to use plain, random words, steer clear of common phrases, such as common quotes, Bible verses, or lines of Shakespeare. Remember – hackers aren’t always people. Instead, they are often algorithms that are trained on large sets of data. To stay ahead of these trained programs, it’s important to keep your password as long and randomized as possible. In addition to making sure your password is strong, it’s important to keep each password unique. Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg learned this in 2016 – both his Pinterest and Twitter passwords were hacked after his LinkedIn password was decrypted. By reusing passwords, you make it easier for hackers to crack multiple accounts with just one login credential. Instead of trying to remember each unique password, use a password manager, such as 1Password or LastPass. With password managers, you will only need to memorize one, unique master password. If a hacker does steal your password, regular changes will prevent continued access to your account. Stolen consumer data often circulates among hacker forums and online black markets for an extended period of time. By keeping your passwords fresh, you will prevent account takeover incidents from occurring. Multi-factor authentication adds an extra level of security to prevent unauthorized access to your account. For example, if you have multi-factor authentication set up with your email, your email service provider will send a text message with a unique code upon each log in. If you enter the code before its expiration, your email service provider will then grant access to your account. For an additional layer of protection, set up a login alert for each account when possible. When someone logs in from an unrecognized location, you will be notified immediately and – if the user is unauthorized - can contact the website administrator to block access. Private information, such as passwords, credit card numbers, social security numbers (SSN), and account numbers, should be guarded with the utmost privacy. Under no circumstances should you ever share such information over email. Furthermore, think twice before sharing your private information with third parties (for example – does your chiropractor really need to know your SSN?). When entering private information into online forms, verify that the website is legitimate and never use your browser to store sensitive information. Avoid using public Wi-Fi to log in to your accounts. If you must use public Wi-Fi, use a virtual private network (VPN) to share data securely. Moreover, be cautious of clicking hyperlinks, even if they’re sent through known sources. Hackers have been known to use popular online quizzes to gain unauthorized access to social media accounts. Unfortunately, no software is perfect – there are vulnerabilities in every system. Keeping your operating systems, browsers, and anti-virus software up-to-date, however, will ensure hackers cannot easily use system flaws to hijack your accounts. Likewise, be sure to apply the same treatment to your mobile devices. Install trusted anti-virus software and ensure all software is updated regularly. Although hackers are becoming increasingly sophisticated with their attacks, multiple layers of protection will help you prevent unauthorized access to your accounts. Remember, your approach to cybersecurity should be defense in depth. While you may not deter every attack, having multiple defenses will significantly decrease the likelihood and magnitude of account takeover fraud.

title: Design Philosophy
summary: Learn the meaning of design philosophy, explore key design guidelines, and see how Polymet can help you
body_text: ​ Introduction It’s a solid, incredible fact about great brands and products: they all rest on a strong design philosophy. That solid backbone that guides every decision from the first draft of layouts to user experience—almost like a compass for the brand creative process. ​ So, what is design philosophy? A design philosophy is a guiding framework that shapes how designers approach every aspect of creating a product or experience. It encompasses the brands’ core beliefs, values, aesthetic principles, targets, and the way they are selected to convey their value. Defining a design philosophy clarifies what matters most in your work. It keeps every choice consistent with your broader vision, from UI elements to broader user flows. ​ Historical Context The concept of a design philosophy is far from new. In fact, it traces back to early 20th-century movements like the Bauhaus school, which championed the unity of form and function as an artistic ideal. Modernist icons like Charles and Ray Eames expanded on these ideas throughout the mid-century, blending playfulness and utility in their work. I’m especially drawn to Dieter Rams at Braun, who famously urged us to embrace “Less, but better.” That wasn’t just a catchy phrase: it was a complete design mindset that stripped away unnecessary frills and distilled complex features into clean, approachable solutions. His meticulous approach laid the groundwork for future product designers—many of whom carried this torch into today’s minimalist wave. Charles and Ray viewed design success through the lens of universal human behaviors rather than individual quirks. This philosophy is exemplified in Charles’s stance that chair design should accommodate natural sitting habits rather than trying to enforce idealized postures. ​ Modern Applications Today, we see design philosophy in companies like Apple, where product design philosophy centers on sleek minimalism and seamless UX design philosophy. Or take Airbnb, which focuses on fostering belonging and community through carefully tailored interfaces. These brands show that a cohesive set of design principles can elevate user experiences, strengthen brand loyalty, and spark creativity. You can read more about Apple’s Design Philosophy here Airbnb Design Philosophy is here ​ Best Practices & Core Principles Every strong design philosophy relies on fundamental design elements—things like color harmonies, typography choices, layout balance, and intuitive workflows. When you stick to these principles of design, you’re able to develop consistent, user-friendly solutions: • Keep visuals coherent: Align your aesthetic with your brand’s voice. • Functionality: Prioritize usability and functional design, as design is how it works. • Stay adaptable: Evolve as user needs, technology, and design trends shift. ​ How to Develop Personal Design Philosophy A personal design philosophy emerges when you reflect on your own values and sources of inspiration: 1) Identify your core interests: Maybe you’re obsessed with clean lines and white space or love bold colors. 2) Take inspiration from the world around you: Find examples of artists, architects, or established design philosophies that align with your taste. But first, inspired by them. 3) Experiment, then refine: Take each concept for a spin, see how it sits with you, and refine your design approach. 4) Adopt new tech responsibly: Innovations in AI can help streamline your process but don’t forget your unique perspective. This self-driven method ensures your philosophy evolves naturally. ​ Impact on Brand & Creativity I’ve seen firsthand how a thoughtful product design philosophy can consistently shape an entire brand identity. People recognize your visuals, trust your process, and get that signature feel the moment they interact with your product. Following carefully defined design guidelines opens up space for creative freedom because everyone is grounded in the same fundamental vision. ​ How Polymet can help you? In today’s AI-driven world, it’s easier than ever to transform ideas into tangible prototypes or production-ready designs. Polymet , an AI product design tool, comes in handy by quickly generating customized pages and components. You can prompt Polymet with your personal design preferences, tweak aspects of the final layout, collaborate with teammates, and share previews. So you can get different examples from just prompts and refine what really reflects you. That is especially powerful if you already have a defined UX design philosophy. Because Polymet respects your foundational design principles, it can create variations that align perfectly with you and your brand’s values. ​ Bringing It All Together Your design philosophy is the soul of your product. With it, you ensure every UI element, page layout, and user interaction exudes the same intentional vibe. Combine that with AI-driven design tools like Polymet, and you’ve got a powerful ally to streamline workflows, remove bottlenecks, and keep your brand identity consistent and compelling. body_text: How to Become a UGC Creator: A Step-by-Step Guide Step 1: Build a Portfolio That Showcases Your Range Starting your journey as a UGC creator requires a solid portfolio that highlights your versatility and authenticity. Brands seek creators who can produce diverse content styles, from quick product demos to detailed reviews or lifestyle integrations. Focus on creating samples that demonstrate your ability to capture genuine reactions, use natural lighting, and tell a story through visuals and audio. Even if you haven’t worked with brands yet, producing self-initiated content with products you own or can borrow will establish your range effectively. This portfolio acts as your calling card, so organize it clearly by content format and style to help brands envision how you can fit into their campaigns. Use free platforms like Instagram, TikTok, or even a simple website to host your portfolio. Keep updating it regularly as your skills improve and trends evolve. Step 2: Define Your Niche and Target Brand Categories Pinpointing your niche sharpens your appeal to specific brands. Instead of targeting every industry, focus on categories where your passion and expertise align with consumer interests. Whether that’s beauty, fitness, tech gadgets, or gaming. Specialization helps you speak the language of that market and produce content that feels informed and relatable. For example, aspiring creators interested in gaming can explore niches related to platforms like Roblox, learning what kind of UGC connects within that community. Choosing a niche also streamlines your portfolio and makes your outreach more targeted. Brands prefer creators who understand their product category intimately and can authentically communicate its value, rather than creators spreading themselves too thin across unrelated industries. Step 3: Choose the Right Platforms for Your Content Deciding where to publish your UGC is critical. Each platform has distinct content formats, audience behaviors, and brand appetites. TikTok, for example, favors short, engaging videos with trending sounds and fast editing, making it ideal for dynamic, informal product showcases. Instagram supports a mix of Reels, Stories, and posts, leaning toward slightly more polished visuals with narrative captions. Understanding these nuances enables you to tailor your creations effectively and increases your chances of discovery by brands seeking creators on those channels. Additionally, some creators find success balancing multiple platforms, while others specialize deeply in one. Evaluate your strengths and resources: producing quality content consistently on platform may be more beneficial than spreading efforts thinly. To accelerate discovery, consider platforms that facilitate creator-brand connections, which is where tools like AI Creator Search play a pivotal role by helping brands find creators who match their criteria quickly. Step 4: Set Competitive Rates Without Underselling Your Work Pricing your UGC services requires balancing market rates with your experience and the value you deliver. New creators often undervalue their work, which can undermine long-term earning potential. Research typical rate ranges within your niche and platform, factoring in content complexity, usage rights, and exclusivity. For example, a single TikTok video with full usage rights commands a different rate than a series of Instagram Stories with limited rights. As you gain experience and brand demand increases, incrementally raise your rates to reflect your growing portfolio and proven results. Communicate your pricing transparently and be prepared to negotiate based on brand budgets. Remember, undervaluing your content sets a precedent that can be difficult to break, so establish rates that respect your time and skill. Step 5: Connect With Brands Through Marketplaces and Direct Outreach Finding your first clients involves proactive outreach and using marketplaces designed for creator-brand matchmaking. Sign up on platforms that aggregate brand campaigns and allow you to pitch your services directly. Additionally, direct outreach via email or social media can open doors if done strategically. Personalize your messages by referencing the brand’s recent campaigns and explaining how your content style aligns with their goals. To optimize your discovery by brands, consider using advanced tools like AI Creator Search . This platform uses natural-language queries and filters by category, engagement, and posting frequency to match creators with brands efficiently. By integrating such AI-powered solutions, you reduce the time spent on manual applications and increase your visibility to high-value clients. title: What Is the Walmart Affiliate Program? A 2026 Guide for Creators
summary: The Walmart affiliate program pays 1-4% standard and up to 18% via Walmart Creator. See commission rates, cookie window, requirements, and payouts for 2026.
body_text: Article Highlights Walmart affiliate program explained: two paths, one goal Standard affiliate pays 1% to 4%; Walmart Creator pays up to 18% Cookie window runs 3 days standard, longer for Creator links No minimum follower count to join Walmart Creator Consistent product videos, not link placement, drive earnings Argil turns one recording into daily product videos The Walmart affiliate program lets you earn a commission when a shopper buys a Walmart product through your tracked link. It runs on two paths. The standard affiliate program through the Impact network pays 1% to 4% by category, and Walmart Creator, built for social creators, pays up to 18% on categories like home decor and beauty. Getting accepted is easy. Earning consistently is the part most people get wrong. What Is the Walmart Affiliate Program? The Walmart affiliate program is a revenue-share arrangement. You share a tracked link to a Walmart product, a shopper clicks it and buys, and Walmart pays you a percentage of that sale. There is no cost to join and no cap on what you can earn ( Walmart Corporate ). There are two paths into it, and confusing them is the first mistake new creators make. The first is the standard affiliate program, run through the Impact partner network. This is the link-based, publisher-oriented setup. It suits bloggers, review-site owners, and anyone who can place product links inside written content on a live website. The second is Walmart Creator, which Walmart launched in beta in October 2022 as a direct answer to the Amazon Influencer program ( Walmart Corporate ). Walmart Creator is built for social creators who post product content on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. It gives you a creator dashboard, product recommendations based on your audience, and access to tens of thousands of products, all with commissions on referred sales and no earnings cap. So who is this for? Bloggers and review-site owners lean toward the standard path. Short-form video creators who can drive product purchases lean toward Walmart Creator. Both reward the same thing in the end, which is people actually buying through your links. Here is the framing the rest of this guide pays off. Approval is the easy part. Walmart Creator has no minimum follower requirement , so almost anyone can get in. The hard part is earning past a few dollars, and that comes down to how much product content you put in front of buyers, not whether you got approved. How the Walmart Affiliate Program Works Commission is paid as a percentage of each qualifying sale, and the percentage depends heavily on which path you are on and which category the product sits in. Commission Rates by Category On the standard affiliate program, affiliates earn between 1% and 4% depending on the product category. That is modest, and it is the number most people quote when they say Walmart pays less than Amazon. Walmart Creator is where the rates get interesting. Home decor, beauty, and apparel pay up to 18% , which is well above what most retail affiliate programs offer. The trade-off is that rates vary widely by category. Media and gaming products sit at the bottom, often paying 0% to 1% , and some items carry no commission at all. The operator read here is simple. Do not build your Walmart affiliate content around electronics and video games, where the rate collapses. Build it around the categories that pay, which are the home, beauty, and apparel products people impulse-buy anyway. A single well-made home organization video sends buyers into an 18% category. A gaming console review sends them into a 1% one, for the same production effort. Cookie Window and Attribution A cookie window is the period after someone clicks your link during which a purchase still credits you. Click today, buy inside the window, you get paid. Buy after it closes, you get nothing. Walmart's standard affiliate program runs a 3-day cookie window , which tracks purchases made within 72 hours of the click. That is shorter than many programs, and it is the second reason Walmart looks less generous than it is on the headline commission. A 3-day window means you are rewarded for driving purchases close to the moment of the click, not for slow-burn consideration buys. This attribution rule quietly reinforces the whole thesis of this guide. A short window rewards volume and recency. The creator posting a fresh product video every day keeps landing clicks that convert inside 72 hours. The creator who dropped one link list last month is relying on a window that closed long ago. Payouts and Thresholds Walmart affiliate commissions are processed through the Impact platform, which pays out by PayPal or direct deposit. On the standard program, payouts run on a monthly basis , typically processed around the 15th for the prior month's earnings, once you clear the minimum balance. Two timing details catch new creators. First, there is a holding period. Because Walmart gives shoppers roughly 30 days to return purchases , your commission is not released the instant a sale lands; it locks first, then pays. Second, reported minimum payout thresholds vary by source and setup, from around $10 up to $50, so confirm your exact threshold inside your own Impact dashboard rather than trusting a blog figure. Do not treat month one as your real income month. Between the return window and the payment cycle, your first meaningful payout often arrives closer to two months after your first sale. Requirements: Who Can Join and How to Apply The eligibility bar for the Walmart affiliate program is low, which is both the appeal and the reason the field is crowded. For Walmart Creator, the basics are straightforward. You must reside in the United States and be at least 18. There is no minimum follower requirement , which is unusual and means you can start promoting products to a small audience immediately. Accepted platforms include Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, blogs, and email newsletters. The standard affiliate path has a different gate. Instead of a social audience, it expects an active website with real, regularly updated, family-friendly content. Review sites and content blogs clear this easily; a bare landing page does not. To apply, here is the order of operations: Decide your path first. Social-video creator goes to Walmart Creator; site owner goes to the standard affiliate program. Have your assets ready before you start: your social handles or website URL, and your tax and payout details for Impact. Submit the application. Approval is fast, often within about a day for the standard program. Once approved, generate tracked links from the dashboard and start placing them in content. The most common rejection reasons are worth self-screening against. Thin or empty websites get declined on the publisher path. Content that violates the family-friendly rule gets declined on both. And an application with no live content to point at, no posts, no site, gives Walmart nothing to approve. Fix those before you apply, not after a rejection. How to Actually Earn: Why Consistent Content Beats Link Placement Here is the part every "how to join the Walmart affiliate program" article skips. Approval and link placement earn almost nothing on their own. Revenue tracks the volume and consistency of product content that puts your links in front of buyers. The mechanics are not mysterious. More product videos mean more tracked clicks. More clicks mean more buying moments landing inside that 3-day window. And a creator who posts steadily gives the platform a reason to keep surfacing their content, which compounds the reach that feeds the whole loop. A single link list sitting in a bio does none of this. The data backs the cadence argument hard. Buffer analyzed 52 million posts and found that creators who posted at least once a week for 20 or more weeks earned 450% more engagement per post than the least consistent group. That is not a rounding-error edge over a slightly higher commission rate. That is the difference between an account that earns and one that stalls. The format that converts is short, single-purpose product videos. A quick haul, one product demo, a "here is how I use this" clip. Each one is a fresh buying moment with a tracked link attached. A once-a-week static post or a bare list of links cannot generate the same click volume, no matter how good the products are. So name the real bottleneck honestly. It is not the affiliate terms, the commission split, or the cookie window. It is that filming a new video for every product, every day, is exhausting and slow. That is where almost every creator quits. They get approved, post for two weeks, run out of filming energy, and the account goes quiet while the 3-day windows close behind them. Producing Daily Product Videos at Scale With Argil This is the exact problem Argil is built to remove. You record a two-minute video of yourself once, and Argil trains an AI clone of you that turns written scripts into fully edited short-form product videos, captions, cuts, and all. Connect that back to the earning argument. The creators who win the Walmart program are the ones who post consistently, and Argil makes daily product video output realistic without filming each one. You keep the cadence the program rewards without spending every evening on camera. The workflow is tight enough to run daily: Write a short script for one product, a demo, a use case, or a quick haul beat. Generate the video with your clone. The editing pipeline handles captions and cuts. Drop in your tracked Walmart link. Publish across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. Repeat tomorrow with the next product. This matters because it is still your face and your voice, produced at a pace a single person could never film manually. That distinction keeps it a personal branding asset rather than a faceless content farm, which is the difference between building an audience that trusts your recommendations and spraying anonymous links no one clicks. Argil starts with a 5-day free trial , then Classic at $39 per month, which is a rounding error against the cost of a video editor if daily posting is what actually drives your Walmart affiliate income. For a deeper look at how creators build a durable presence on camera without burning out, our guide to personal brand examples that actually drive business covers what changes when AI handles production. And if you are weighing the broader "post daily without filming daily" question, how to create video content without being on camera walks through the options. FAQ How much does the Walmart affiliate program pay? It depends on your path and category. The standard affiliate program pays 1% to 4% by category through the Impact network. Walmart Creator pays up to 18% on high-value categories like home decor, beauty, and apparel, dropping to 0% to 1% on media and gaming products. Do you need a website to join the Walmart affiliate or Creator program? For the standard affiliate program, yes, you need an active, family-friendly website with real content. Walmart Creator works differently. It accepts social platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, so short-form creators can join without a blog. How long is the Walmart affiliate cookie window? The standard Walmart affiliate program uses a 3-day (72-hour) cookie window, meaning a purchase credits you only if it happens within three days of the click. Confirm the current window for your specific link type inside your Impact dashboard. How do you get paid, and what is the minimum payout threshold? Payments run through Impact by PayPal or direct deposit on a monthly cycle. Reported minimum thresholds vary from around $10 to $50 depending on source and setup, and commissions lock for roughly 30 days to cover returns before they release, so check your exact threshold in your own dashboard. Can you do the Walmart affiliate program with only short-form video and no blog? Yes. Walmart Creator was built for exactly this. You link products directly from social posts and reels, no website required. The catch is that video-first creators live or die on posting cadence, since each video is a fresh buying moment. Approves Regulatory Submission of New 10% Repurchase Program 07/29/2026 Download (opens in new window) GRAND ISLAND, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Central Plains Bancshares, Inc. Upon adoption, the repurchase program would replace the Company’s current repurchase program. About Central Plains Bancshares, Inc. Central Plains Bancshares, Inc. is the holding company for Home Federal Savings and Loan Association of Grand Island, which operates under the name “Home Federal Bank.” Originally chartered in 1935, Home Federal Bank is a federally-chartered stock savings association headquartered in Grand Island, Nebraska. The Bank conducts its operations from the main office in Grand Island, Nebraska, eight branch offices located in Grand Island, Hastings, Holdrege, Lexington, Lincoln and Superior, Nebraska, and a drive-up facility in Grand Island, Nebraska. title: OKYO Pharma Announces Purchase of Shares by Chief Development Officer and Director
summary: Gary S. Jacob, PhD, Chief Development Officer and Director of OKYO Pharma has increased his holdings with the purchase of 3,500 of the Company’s ordinary shares on NASDAQ at $1.40 per share, bringing his total holding to 112,420 ordinary shares.
body_text: London and New York, NY, July 22, 2026. OKYO Pharma Limited (Nasdaq: OKYO ), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing investigational therapies for the treatment of neuropathic corneal pain (NCP) and anterior segment eye diseases, today announced that Gary S. Jacob, PhD, Chief Development Officer and Director of OKYO Pharma has increased his holdings with the purchase of 3,500 of the Company’s ordinary shares on NASDAQ at $1.40 per share, bringing his total holding to 112,420 ordinary shares. About OKYO Pharma OKYO Pharma Limited (Nasdaq: OKYO) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative therapies for the treatment of neuropathic corneal pain (NCP) and anterior segment eye diseases, with ordinary shares listed for trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market. OKYO plans to initiate a global Phase 3 pivotal clinical trial in the second half of this year, enrolling approximately 111 patients to evaluate a single-dose regimen of urcosimod for the treatment of NCP. For further information, please visit www.okyopharma.com . title: Danielle Friedman Joins Well as a Fitness Reporter
body_text: A longtime freelance contributor, Danielle will bring her deep fitness expertise to the Well desk. Read more below from Lori Leibovich, Blake Wilson and Molly Mirhashem. We’re thrilled to announce that Danielle Friedman is joining the Well desk as a reporter covering fitness, a beat that is central to our desk’s mission and very popular with our readers. Danielle has spent more than two decades covering health, science, gender and culture. For the past four years, she has been a regular contributor to Well, reporting on the personalities and trends shaping fitness culture and translating the latest exercise science into actionable advice. She has written some of our most well-read fitness stories, including delightful profiles of the 102-year-old French yoga teacher Charlotte Chopin and the “Slow AF Run Club” founder Martinus Evans and an interactive feature about the decade that changed fitness forever. As the author of the 2022 book “ Let’s Get Physical: How Women Discovered Exercise and Reshaped the World ,” a history of women and fitness, she brings a depth and breadth of knowledge about the origins of contemporary fitness culture to her reporting. She has also reported on women’s health and race and gender disparities in medicine and wellness. Danielle was previously a senior editor at NBC News Digital and The Daily Beast and a nonfiction editor at Penguin Books. She is a graduate of Duke University and Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism. She is also a proud slow runner and is currently training for her fourth marathon. Danielle starts July 20. Please join us in welcoming her to Well! — Lori, Blake and Molly
